research_mode: official Home Office accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.name: Release scope
verified_claims: The Home Office release was published on 22 July 2026 and reports police workforce statistics as at 31 March 2026 for England and Wales.
limitations: The publication is a workforce snapshot and does not measure incidents or risk at an individual parcel.

sources.name: Force coverage
verified_claims: The release covers the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales and reports British Transport Police figures separately.
limitations: Force-area workforce coverage is not exact-address or parcel-level evidence.

sources.name: Worker-type coverage
verified_claims: The release covers police officers, police staff, designated officers, PCSOs, special constables and police support volunteers.
limitations: Worker counts describe organisational capacity rather than local incident exposure.

sources.name: Total paid workforce
verified_claims: There were 234,441 FTE paid police workers in the 43 territorial forces as at 31 March 2026.
limitations: A national workforce total cannot identify conditions around a particular property.

sources.name: Total workforce annual change
verified_claims: The total paid workforce decreased by 1,332 FTE, or 0.6%, compared with March 2025.
limitations: A year-on-year staffing change is not a parcel-level public-safety score.

sources.name: Workforce gap from peak
verified_claims: The March 2026 total workforce was 10,056 FTE, or 4.1%, below the March 2010 peak.
limitations: A historical staffing comparison does not establish local causation or risk.

sources.name: Territorial police officers
verified_claims: There were 145,886 FTE police officers in the 43 territorial forces as at 31 March 2026.
limitations: The figure is an aggregate headcount-equivalent measure and cannot be assigned to a parcel.

sources.name: Police officer annual change
verified_claims: Police officer numbers decreased by 566 FTE, or 0.4%, compared with March 2025.
limitations: National workforce movement cannot substitute for local incident data.

sources.name: Police officer gap from peak
verified_claims: Police officer numbers were 1,859 FTE, or 1.3%, below the March 2024 peak.
limitations: A gap from a national peak is not evidence about a neighbourhood or address.

sources.name: British Transport Police officers
verified_claims: British Transport Police employed 2,817 FTE police officers in England and Wales as at 31 March 2026.
limitations: BTP staffing is reported separately and cannot be attributed to a land parcel.

sources.name: National Crime Agency officers
verified_claims: The release reports 5,540 FTE National Crime Agency officers in England and Wales.
limitations: NCA staffing is not a measure of crime prevalence around a property.

sources.name: Central-services secondments
verified_claims: There were 350 FTE police officers seconded to central services.
limitations: Secondment totals are organisational data, not geographic public-safety evidence.

sources.name: Special constables
verified_claims: There were 5,196 special constables on a headcount basis in the 43 territorial forces.
limitations: Special constable headcount has no contracted-hours denominator and is not parcel evidence.

sources.name: Police support volunteers
verified_claims: There were 6,035 police support volunteers on a headcount basis in the 43 territorial forces.
limitations: Volunteer headcount does not indicate service intensity or local incident risk.

sources.name: Police staff and designated officers
verified_claims: There were 81,296 FTE police staff and designated officers as at 31 March 2026.
limitations: Staffing levels are organisational aggregates and cannot score a parcel.

sources.name: Staff annual change
verified_claims: Police staff and designated officer numbers decreased by 710 FTE, or 0.9%, from March 2025.
limitations: Annual staffing change does not establish local service availability at an address.

sources.name: Staff gap from peak
verified_claims: Police staff and designated officer numbers were 2,140 FTE, or 2.6%, below the March 2010 peak.
limitations: Historical national comparison is not a local risk measure.

sources.name: PCSO total
verified_claims: There were 7,259 FTE PCSOs as at 31 March 2026.
limitations: PCSO totals are not neighbourhood incident counts and cannot be parcel-attributed.

sources.name: PCSO annual change
verified_claims: PCSO numbers decreased by 55 FTE, or 0.8%, compared with March 2025.
limitations: A national change does not describe conditions at a specific location.

sources.name: PCSO gap from peak
verified_claims: PCSO numbers were 9,658 FTE, or 57.1%, below the March 2010 peak.
limitations: A long-term workforce gap cannot be converted into an address-level safety score.

sources.name: Special constable annual change
verified_claims: Special constable headcount decreased by 324, or 5.9%, compared with March 2025.
limitations: The change is a national workforce statistic, not parcel evidence.

sources.name: Frontline officer share
verified_claims: As at 31 March 2026, 90.5% of police officers were recorded in frontline roles.
limitations: Frontline classification is based on primary role and does not measure all activity around a parcel.

sources.name: Frontline officer total
verified_claims: There were 115,764 FTE police officers recorded in frontline roles as at 31 March 2026.
limitations: A national frontline total cannot establish local response capacity for an exact address.

sources.name: Frontline annual change
verified_claims: Frontline officer numbers decreased by 1,518 FTE, or 1.3%, from March 2025.
limitations: National year-on-year change is not a parcel-specific service metric.

sources.name: Frontline gap from peak
verified_claims: The March 2026 frontline total was 7,701 FTE below the March 2023 peak.
limitations: A workforce peak comparison cannot be used as direct local-risk evidence.

sources.name: Local policing function
verified_claims: There were 55,561 FTE officers in Local policing roles, accounting for 43.4% of officers.
limitations: Function allocation reflects primary duties and cannot identify coverage at one parcel.

sources.name: Investigations function
verified_claims: There were 23,676 FTE officers in Investigations roles, accounting for 18.5% of officers.
limitations: Investigation staffing is not a local crime or response-time measure.

sources.name: Primary-role convention
verified_claims: Functions statistics classify workers by the primary role in which they spend most of their time.
limitations: The classification may omit secondary duties and must not be overinterpreted for parcel scoring.

sources.name: Functions framework comparability
verified_claims: Functions data from 2015 onward use the CIPFA Police Objective Analysis framework and are not directly comparable with the earlier framework.
limitations: Framework changes limit long-run comparisons and prevent unqualified local inference.

sources.name: Student-officer guidance
verified_claims: Guidance clarified that student officers in classroom-based training should be recorded in the Other function group.
limitations: The recording change affects comparability and does not reflect a sudden local operational change.
